c1: “Community benefits valued at $761 million include significant traffic and roadway improvements, improvements to the Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA)’s public transit station, over 25 acres of new public open space, a Community Impact Fund, and funding for neighborhood social services.”
https://bloximages.chicago2.vip.townnews.com/pressofatlanticcity.com/content/tncms/assets/v3/editorial/4/5b/45beb9c7-dd44-4850-b206-d4f0249b219b/692dd87b17ea4.pdf.pdf

c2: “HRMP proposes extensive traffic and roadway improvements, including ADA-compliant upgrades to the Willets Point MTA subway station, reconfigured intersections, new pedestrian and bicycle paths, and improved access to public transit.”
https://bloximages.chicago2.vip.townnews.com/pressofatlanticcity.com/content/tncms/assets/v3/editorial/4/5b/45beb9c7-dd44-4850-b206-d4f0249b219b/692dd87b17ea4.pdf.pdf

c3: “Hard Rock Metropolitan Park has engaged with the MTA for over three years about the proposed improvements at Mets-Willets Point, and the MTA provided conceptual approval of the Proposed Improvements at the 30% Construction Documents stage of review in a letter dated August 21, 2024”
https://nycasinos.ny.gov/system/files/documents/2025/09/cac-mta-questions-response-redacted-c-1.pdf

c4: “We have and will continue to work in good faith to secure all necessary approvals from the MTA and meet all necessary deadlines to deliver this required community benefit.”
https://nycasinos.ny.gov/system/files/documents/2025/09/cac-mta-questions-response-redacted-c-1.pdf

c5: “Resorts World NYC is already generating gaming revenue and expanding its casino floor, while Hard Rock Metropolitan Park in Queens and Bally’s Bronx continue through development, financing, construction, and permitting stages.”
https://www.actionnetwork.com/news/new-york-casino-resorts-world-hard-rock-ballys-update/

c6: “$163 million for a Community Impact Fund that will provide grants to non -profit organizations serving Queens communities and residents.”
https://www1.nyc.gov/assets/planning/download/pdf/about/cpc/250046.pdf

c7: “A $163 million Community Benefits Fund (with the understanding this Fund should be increased) to be accessible for 30 years (or until the funds are depleted) and allocated across local Queens Community Districts 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, and 9;”
https://www1.nyc.gov/assets/planning/download/pdf/about/cpc/250046.pdf

c8: “A Community Advisory Board that will meet regularly and act as a watchdog for all promised community benefits;”
https://www1.nyc.gov/assets/planning/download/pdf/about/cpc/250046.pdf

c9: “$25 million for community identified health care and youth and senior needs, including a health clinic in East Elmhurst , a youth and senior center in Corona, and addiction and mental health services infrastructure in Flushing.”
https://www1.nyc.gov/assets/planning/download/pdf/about/cpc/250046.pdf
